report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of daedalus/eval/harness.py: arms aggregate, run_arms, tier2, provider detection, baseline load/snapshot/write. Claims mostly kept; two uncheckable due to out-of-chunk references.
risks: run_arms | medium | _correctness_task_row may not include 'focus_withheld' or 'error' keys, but code filters on them; if absent, tasks are treated as healthy. | Verify _correctness_task_row output includes those keys.

run_tier2 | medium | _whole_repo_text called twice per repo (capped and uncapped); if it is not idempotent or expensive, double work; also tokens_B_true may be inconsistent if repo changes between calls. | Inspect _whole_repo_text implementation.
run_tier2 | low | _ask catches all exceptions and returns empty string; empty answer may be scored as success if answer_contains is empty. | Check task answer_contains invariants.
snapshot_baseline | medium | Snapshot contains label_provenance and tier fields but run_gate may expect different keys; schema version is 1 but no validation. | Check run_gate's expected schema.

write_baseline | low | The docstring claims deterministic formatting (sorted keys) but the chunk does not show the write call; json.dump may not sort by default. | Inspect the write call after line 561.
detect_provider | low | Probe uses urllib.request.urlopen without explicit timeout for DNS resolution; may hang beyond 2s. | Test with unreachable host.
detect_provider | low | If OLLAMA_MODEL is set but not in models, silently falls back to first model, possibly surprising. | Check callers' expectations.
todos: Confirm write_baseline uses sorted keys (json.dump sort_keys=True).
Check run_gate's expected baseline schema and snapshot fields.

handoff.purpose: Arms aggregation, Tier 2 LLM comparison, provider detection, baseline load/snapshot/write.

symbols.name: _arms_aggregate
symbols.note: Aggregates per-task arm rows into summary counts and means.

symbols.name: run_arms
symbols.note: Runs A/B/C comparison over tasks, using cached index and chunks; handles correctness tasks and errors.

symbols.name: _score
symbols.note: Checks if all expected substrings appear case-insensitively; returns success bool and fraction.

symbols.name: detect_provider
symbols.note: Probes local Ollama /api/tags with 2s timeout; returns provider descriptor or None.

symbols.name: _ask
symbols.note: Sends single LLM chat completion via OpenAI-compatible endpoint; never raises, returns empty string on failure.

symbols.name: run_tier2
symbols.note: Opt-in Tier 2 comparison of distilled slice vs whole-repo concat; skips if no provider; tracks truncated B and true token counts.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH
symbols.note: Path to baseline.json next to this file.

symbols.name: load_baseline
symbols.note: Reads baseline.json or returns empty baseline if missing.

symbols.name: snapshot_baseline
symbols.note: Builds baseline structure from run_tier1 results, excluding errored and focus-withheld tasks; does not write disk.

symbols.name: write_baseline
symbols.note: Writes baseline to disk using snapshot_baseline; explicit-only per docstring; returns path.

claims.text: Model-free (recall via _recall), offline, no LLM -- safe to run alongside Tier 1.
claims.why: run_arms calls _recall (via eval_task_arms) and does not invoke _ask or any LLM; it only uses cached_index and _repo_chunks.

claims.text: See eval_task_arms for what each arm measures and by_provenance for the (never-blended) per-provenance-tier breakdown.
claims.why: eval_task_arms and by_provenance are defined elsewhere; this chunk cannot verify their contents.

claims.text: if C ties or beats A ... that is reported loudly, not smoothed over
claims.why: c_beats_a uses >=, so ties are counted as beats; comment explicitly explains the tie-inclusive choice.

claims.text: Tie-inclusive on purpose: a strict '>' here silently counted a BM25 tie as an A win, contradicting the 'C>=A' column header (report.py) and this function's own docstring
claims.why: The claim refers to report.py's column header and the function's docstring, neither of which is present in this chunk.

claims.text: recall_A==1.0 on every current hand_reachable task makes a strict C win impossible, so with '>' the tie case -- dumb retrieval matching the product at equal cost, the commercially damning one -- was the ONLY case that could ever fire and it was being absorbed into 'no'.
claims.why: This claim depends on actual task data (recall_A values) and the definition of hand_reachable; not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Success = every expected substring appears (case-insensitive). Also return the fraction present for a softer signal.
claims.why: The code lowercases answer and each substring, checks presence, returns (present == len, present/len).

claims.text: Only a local Ollama HTTP endpoint is probed (free, no key, no egress). The probe is a 2s GET to /api/tags -- it does nothing unless Tier 2 is requested.
claims.why: The function only probes when called (run_tier2 calls it); it uses urlopen with timeout=2 to host + '/api/tags'; no other network calls.

claims.text: Single text-only turn against the provider. Never raises to the caller.
claims.why: The entire body is wrapped in try/except Exception, returning '' on any failure; it sends one chat_completion call.

claims.text: Opt-in Tier 2. Compares distilled-slice (A) vs whole-repo-concat (B) task success + tokens. Cleanly skipped (never crashes) when no provider is up.
claims.why: If detect_provider returns None, returns a skipped dict immediately; otherwise proceeds with semantic_slice and whole text; errors are caught per task.

claims.text: B's tokens were ALREADY measured with the real tokenizer before this change (count_tokens is exact whenever tiktoken is installed) -- that part was honest.
claims.why: The claim about 'before this change' and tiktoken exactness cannot be verified from this chunk; count_tokens is imported but its implementation is elsewhere.

claims.text: What was NOT honest: B is capped at cap_tokens * 4 chars before being measured, so tokens_B silently reflected a TRUNCATED text, not the real whole-repo size.
claims.why: The code sets cap_chars = cap_tokens * 4 and calls _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars) to get ctx_b; tokens_B is count_tokens(ctx_b) on the truncated text.

claims.text: tokens_B_true (added here) is the untruncated whole-repo token count, so a truncated B can never be mistaken for the real baseline.
claims.why: The code calls _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars=None) to get full_text and counts tokens with count_tokens(full_text), storing in tokens_B_true.

claims.text: Read baseline.json, or an empty baseline if it does not exist yet (a fresh repo checkout before the first --update-baseline run).
claims.why: If os.path.exists(p) is False, returns {'schema': 1, 'tasks': {}}; otherwise reads and json.loads.

claims.text: Pure: build the baseline structure for the CURRENT recall of tasks (default TASKS). Does not touch disk -- see write_baseline.
claims.why: The function only calls run_tier1 and builds a dict; no file I/O in this function.

claims.text: Every task is snapshotted (including quarantine ones) so quarantine promotion is still comparable later; only PRIMARY tasks are ever gated (see run_gate).
claims.why: This chunk does not show quarantine handling nor run_gate; cannot verify that all tasks are snapshotted or that gating is primary-only.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (run_tier1) have no recall to snapshot and are skipped here -- they simply get no baseline entry, which makes them a 'new task' (not silently a pass) the next time run_gate sees them resolve successfully.
claims.why: The dict comprehension filters out tasks where 'error' in t, so errored tasks get no entry.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file) are skipped for the same reason: there is no recall key to snapshot, and re-baselining a fence-refused task would silently launder 'never measured' into 'passing'.
claims.why: The comprehension filters out t.get('focus_withheld'), so such tasks are excluded.

claims.text: EXPLICIT-ONLY baseline write. Never call this from an automatic code path -- a baseline that updates itself is not a ratchet, it is a no-op. Only the '--update-baseline' CLI flag (a human decision) should reach this.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the CLI flag or any callers; cannot verify that only the flag reaches this function.

claims.text: Returns the path written. Deterministic formatting (sorted keys) so the diff is meaningful in review.
claims.why: The function body is truncated at the open() call; the return and json.dump call are not visible, so deterministic formatting cannot be confirmed.

observations.what: _arms_aggregate uses _mean on lists that could be empty if n=0; _mean may divide by zero.
c_beats_a uses >=, which is intentional per comment; but the comment is long and may be mistaken for a defect by future readers.
run_tier2 calls _whole_repo_text twice per repo (capped and uncapped); if _whole_repo_text is expensive or not idempotent, this doubles work and may produce inconsistent results.
detect_provider uses urllib.request.urlopen without a socket-level timeout; DNS resolution could hang beyond the 2s timeout.
snapshot_baseline stores 'label_provenance' and 'tier' but run_gate may expect different field names; schema version 1 is not validated.
write_baseline's docstring claims deterministic formatting but the actual write call is not shown; json.dump may not sort keys unless sort_keys=True.
run_arms filters on 'focus_withheld' and 'error' keys; if _correctness_task_row does not include those keys, correctness tasks may be misclassified as healthy.
